title: James Webb telescope finds ice older than the star it orbits
summary: Radiation and collisions reshape the planetary building materials.
llm_summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has detected water‑ice grains in a distant planetary system that are older than the star they orbit, showing that the raw material for planets can survive from earlier generations of stars. The findings suggest that intense radiation and high‑speed collisions continuously re‑process and recycle
